claims.text: Madras’s municipal accounts describe court and tax powers. Aitchison’s editorial account describes Krishna Raj Wadiar’s 1799 subsidiary treaty, force, subsidy and conditional British intervention. Bengaluru’s district account distinguishes Maharaja-administered old Bangalore from the British cantonment outside it in 1809. These are different institutions, not uniform direct rule or consent.

claims.text: What local evidence prevents a Mysore treaty from becoming blanket direct rule over Bangalore? The district account distinguishes old Bangalore’s Maharaja administration and a British cantonment outside it; the treaty compiler describes a conditional military/fiscal relationship, not identical municipal powers everywhere.

recall.question: What local evidence prevents a Mysore treaty from becoming blanket direct rule over Bangalore?
options: Old Bangalore’s Maharaja administration differed from the British cantonment outside it.
The treaty immediately placed all of Bangalore under one direct administration.
recall.why: The district account distinguishes old Bangalore’s Maharaja administration and a British cantonment outside it; the treaty compiler describes a conditional military/fiscal relationship, not identical municipal powers everywhere.

care: Named Mysore ruler and conditional relationship remain attached; distinguish city/cantonment and compiler account from treaty text.
